title: (Senior) Backend Engineer C++ (All genders)
description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost effective. This provides our operators with a decisive edge in highly contested environments.
We’re focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems - not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe - today.

About the team

Minerva is STARK's command and control software — the brain that connects operators to autonomous systems across multiple domains in real time. The Minerva team is a small, senior software group based in Berlin and Munich, working directly with our systems and hardware teams to build mission-critical C2 capabilities deployed in active operational environments.We move fast, ship real software, and operate under constraints most engineers never encounter — low-bandwidth networks, air-gapped devices, high-stakes decision loops. There is no room for abstraction for its own sake. Everything we build ends up in the hands of real operators in the field.

Your mission

This is not a "standard" backend role. You won't be building CRUD apps for a web store. You will be building the high-performance, low-latency engine at the heart of Minerva Frontline, our Command & Control (C2) Software, enabling mission planning and operations of Aerial and Maritime asset swarms in real world conditions.
We are looking for C++ developers to build out our core server-side architecture enabling the increasingly complex CONOPS required by NATO’s Armed forces. You will be responsible for how we maintain a global battlefield state, how we translate high-level operator intents into machine-executable actions, and how we stream real-time telemetry to the frontline.
You will work in a high-density engineering environment alongside robotics, safety, and mission planning experts. If you care about RAII, memory safety, and squeezing every ounce of performance out of real hardware in the field to ensure mission success, this is the role.
What You'll Build

- The System Brain: You will develop the core C++ services that orchestrate UAV and USV swarms, maintaining a synchronized and robust battlefield state across distributed systems.
- Mission Control APIs: You will design and implement high-performance gRPC and REST APIs that bridge the gap between our frontend C2 interface and the autonomous vehicles in the field.
- Real-Time Data Pipelines: You will build and optimize the telemetry pipelines that handle high-frequency data from diverse sensors, ensuring low-latency synchronization and delivery.
- Scalable Architecture: You will expand our current C++ architecture to support "affordable mass"—scaling from controlling 4 to 20+ vehicles simultaneously.
- Tactical Integration: You will implement military standards and protocols (such as STANAG), ensuring our systems are interoperable and battle-ready.
- Robustness & Testing: You will build and maintain the test suites, ensuring our code performs reliably under the most contested conditions.

Responsibilities

- A C++ Native: You write clean, performant Modern C++ (17/20/23). You understand the cost of every allocation and the value of a deterministic system.
- Systems-Minded: You think in terms of data flows, state machines, and concurrency. You understand that in our domain, "late data is wrong data."
- A Problem Solver: You dive deep into the details to identify, understand, and solve difficult technical problems at the hardware-software boundary.
- High Agency: You don't wait for perfect specifications. You understand the mission, look at the code, and drive the architecture forward.
- Collaborative: You thrive in a multidisciplinary team, working closely with frontend, robotics, and integration engineers to deliver a cohesive product.

Qualifications

- Experience: 5+ years of experience in backend or systems engineering, with a primary focus on high-performance C++ applications.
- C++ Expertise: Deep proficiency in Modern C++ (17 or later).
- Networking: Strong understanding of asynchronous networking, inter-process communication (IPC), and real-time data streaming.
- Industry Context: Relevant experience in Aerospace, Robotics, Automotive, Sensors, or High-Frequency Trading—any domain where software interacts with the physical world in real-time.
- Bonus Skills: Familiarity with autopilot/flight control systems (MAVLink/PX4/ArduPilot), geospatial data handling (GIS), or building safety-critical software systems.

Why Join STARK?

- Impact: Build the software that NATO militaries rely on when stakes are highest. Your code will directly influence the outcome of critical missions.
- Engineering Excellence: Work in a culture where technical rigor and architectural beauty are valued. We don't cut corners on safety or performance.
- Novelty: Solve "Genesis-stage" engineering problems for autonomous swarming that have no off-the-shelf solution.
- Growth: As we scale our platforms from the North Sea to the edges of Europe, your role and impact on the organization will grow with us.

If interested in this opportunity, send us your CV in English, and we will reach out to you soon!

- Create Data Tooling: Build the programmatic tools that bridge raw data and downstream usage. This includes writing services to automatically sub-sample video feeds, extract valuable frames, package datasets, and build self-serve data access tools.

- Database & Metadata Engineering: Design, implement, and maintain our metadata databases and data catalogs (tracking datasets, recordings, sensors, labels, and lineage) using solid SQL and schema design principles.

- Data Operations & Labeling Workflows: Own the end-to-end technical workflows for data curation and labeling. You will build the operational tooling and coordinate with external labeling subcontractors to ensure high-quality data deliveries, track progress, and run automated QA.

- Generalist Problem Solving: Thrive in an evolving startup environment. Take on ambiguous problems, migrate legacy data, handle access management, and aggressively automate away manual support tasks.

- Data Engineering & ETL: Proven experience designing, building, and operating robust ETL/data ingestion pipelines.

- Database Mastery: Solid SQL (PostgreSQL preferred) with a strong grasp of schema design, data modeling, and metadata systems.

- Pragmatic & Adaptable: You know how to balance a quick, scrappy fix with a long-term architectural solution, and you are highly comfortable with the changing priorities of a startup environment.

- Communicator & Coordinator: You are comfortable working cross-functionally and coordinating with external vendors and non-technical stakeholders to drive data labeling and curation efforts.

- Data Ecosystems: Familiarity with data versioning (DVC, LakeFS, FiftyOne), computer vision annotation formats (e.g., COCO), or large-scale data curation workflows.

- Advanced GCP: Experience with GCP services beyond basic storage (BigQuery, Cloud Run, IAM).

- Robotics / Complex Data: Exposure to robotics data formats (ROS bags, MCAP, PX4 logs) or handling heavy, multi-modal data streams (video, lidar).

A note on our process: we value critical thinking, grit, and the ability to learn over a perfect checklist. If you don't hit every bullet point but you love building data systems that real engineers depend on every day, we still want to hear from you.

Your mission

You are the technical owner of our multi-sensor recording systems — the bridge between raw hardware and the datasets our ML teams train on. You work at the critical intersection of hardware and software: integrating EO/IR cameras, lidar, radar, and IMUs over their real interfaces, adapting the drivers and ROS2 nodes that capture them, solving time synchronization down to the microsecond, and calibrating multi-sensor rigs so every stream is spatially and temporally unified. Responsibilities

- Own the end-to-end integration of our sensor suites — EO/IR cameras, gimbals, lidar, radar, IMU, GNSS — from electrical interfaces and wiring to working recording pipelines

- Design and implement sensor drivers and ROS2 nodes, working directly with hardware protocols including I2C, SPI, CAN, Serial, MIPI/CSI-2, GigE Vision, and Ethernet (RTSP/UDP)

- Solve temporal synchronization across distributed sensors (PTP, PPS, hardware triggering) so all streams are perfectly aligned for fusion and labeling

- Develop and execute rigorous intrinsic and extrinsic calibration routines (camera-camera, camera-IMU) to spatially unify the sensor rigs

- Build and optimize the onboard recording stack on embedded compute (NVIDIA Jetson): hardware-accelerated video pipelines (GStreamer), efficient logging (MCAP/rosbag), and storage throughput under compute, thermal, and bandwidth constraints

- Evaluate new sensors hands-on at the bench — from probing electrical interfaces with diagnostic tools to benchmarking SDKs — and turn results into clear integration decisions

- Join field data-collection campaigns across Europe: prepare and verify sensor setups, operate the recording systems on-site, diagnose hardware and software issues in real time, and validate recordings before leaving the site

- Produce integration documentation and calibration reports so every setup is reproducible by the team

Qualifications

- Degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or comparable practical experience

- Proficiency in Python and C++ for robotics and hardware interfacing

- Experience with ROS2, including deployment on physical systems

- Hands-on experience with several hardware protocols such as I2C, SPI, CAN, Serial, or Ethernet-based sensor communication

- Experience integrating cameras or other sensors on embedded Linux platforms, ideally NVIDIA Jetson

- Solid computer vision fundamentals: camera models, distortion, projection geometry, OpenCV

- Good understanding of coordinate frames, transformations, and time synchronization in distributed systems — practical calibration experience is a strong plus

- Comfortable with hardware diagnostic tools (multimeter, oscilloscope) as well as modern software workflows (Git, CI, Docker)

- Practical and structured; willingness to travel regularly for field campaigns and to work outdoors in various conditions

Nice to have

- UAV or mobile robot experience; PX4/ArduPilot and MAVLink basics

- Photogrammetry + 3D Reconstruction

- Low-level driver development or customization on embedded Linux

- GStreamer hardware-accelerated pipelines, JetPack/L4T, CUDA/TensorRT

- MIPI/CSI-2 camera bring-up, ISP tuning, or Linux kernel/device tree exposure

- Calibration tooling such as Kalibr; lidar and point cloud processing (PCL, Open3D)

- Experience with detection/tracking models and modern CV pipelines (PyTorch, ONNX)

- Experience with simulation (Gazebo, Isaac Sim) or synthetic data generation

We hire this role across experience levels: whether you bring a few years of hands-on robotics work or a decade of sensor integration, we will match scope and seniority to your profile.

A note on our process: we value critical thinking, grit, and the ability to learn over a perfect checklist. If you are a talented engineer who loves building complex systems at the boundary of hardware and code, but you don't hit every single bullet point, we still want to hear from you.

Our perception team is responsible for the "eyes and inner ear" of STARK's unmanned aerial vehicles. We are a multidisciplinary group of hardware, optical, and software engineers dedicated to integrating cutting-edge sensors into resource-constrained platforms. As a member of this team, you will collaborate closely with mechanical designers and autonomy engineers in a fast-paced, hands-on environment. As a Sensor Systems Engineer, you will be the architect of our platforms' physical perception systems, focusing heavily on the integration of EO/IR cameras, IMUs, and Lidar. You will take ownership of the entire hardware lifecycle, from defining optical specifications to debugging high-speed electrical interfaces in the lab. - Navigate complex design trade-offs with cross-functional teams to balance optical resolution against strict weight, thermal, and power constraints.

- Deep understanding of applied optics, including lens selection, camera architectures, sensor formats, and radiometric performance.

- Experience handling hardware suppliers, vetting vendor specifications, and driving technical procurement decisions.

- Strong foundational knowledge of imaging systems (EO and IR cameras) and Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs).

description:

Minerva is STARK's command and control software — the brain that connects operators to autonomous systems across multiple domains in real time. The Minerva team is a small, senior software group based in Berlin and Munich, working directly with our systems and hardware teams to build mission-critical C2 capabilities deployed in active operational environments.We move fast, ship real software, and operate under constraints most engineers never encounter — low-bandwidth networks, air-gapped devices, high-stakes decision loops. There is no room for abstraction for its own sake. Everything we build ends up in the hands of real operators in the field.

Your mission

Support the development, integration, testing, and operational use of tactical data link capabilities for STARK’s unmanned systems, Ground Control Stations, and wider command-and-control environments. You will help ensure that our systems can communicate reliably and securely with military networks, command posts, allied platforms, and mission systems. A key part of the role is to evaluate, understand, and integrate tactical communication standards and technologies such as Link 16, Link 22, SATCOM, and other military data link solutions. You will translate operational communication requirements into practical integration concepts, test setups, and deployable system configurations.

Responsibilities

Tactical Data Link Integration: Support the integration of tactical data link capabilities such as Link 16, Link 22, SATCOM, and other military communication systems into STARK platforms and Ground Control Station environments.

Interoperability Concepts: Define and support communication concepts that enable reliable data exchange between unmanned systems, GCS setups, command centers, allied platforms, and external mission systems.

Requirements Translation: Translate operational and military communication requirements into technical integration requirements, interface definitions, test needs, and subsystem-level implementation concepts.

System Interface Support: Work with engineering, software, network, RF, modem, antenna, and GCS teams to align interfaces, protocols, data flows, configuration requirements, and integration constraints.

SATCOM & Beyond-Line-of-Sight Support: Support concepts and integration activities for SATCOM, long-range communication paths, and other beyond-line-of-sight connectivity options.

Testing & Validation: Plan and support lab tests, field tests, interoperability checks, and validation activities for tactical data link and communication setups.

Security & Reliability: Contribute to secure, robust, and mission-ready communication architectures, considering availability, latency, data integrity, authentication, and operational constraints.

Supplier & Partner Coordination: Work with external suppliers, partners, military stakeholders, and internal teams to assess data link options, integration dependencies, and technical feasibility.

Documentation: Document data link concepts, interface assumptions, configuration settings, integration dependencies, test results, and recommended operational setups in a clear and maintainable way.

Qualifications

Experience: Around 5 years of professional experience in tactical communications, military data links, SATCOM, RF systems, communication engineering, systems engineering, or a related technical field.

Tactical Data Link Knowledge: Practical understanding of military data link technologies such as Link 16, Link 22, SATCOM, or comparable tactical communication systems.

Systems Understanding: Ability to understand complex communication architectures involving platforms, radios, antennas, modems, networks, command systems, software interfaces, and operational workflows.

Interoperability Mindset: Strong understanding of how different systems exchange data, how interfaces are defined, and how interoperability is tested and validated.

Technical Communication: Ability to translate between operational users, engineering teams, software developers, RF specialists, suppliers, and program stakeholders.

Testing & Documentation: Experience supporting technical tests, integration trials, validation activities, or operational demonstrations, including structured documentation of results and findings.

Problem-Solving Ability: Strong analytical mindset with the ability to identify communication issues, integration gaps, configuration problems, and practical solutions.

Communication: Solid English skills are required. German skills for technical communication, stakeholder alignment, and documentation are a plus.

Team Fit: Ability to work collaboratively in a small, cross-functional team and communicate clearly and reliably in fast-moving engineering environments.

Clearance: Ability to obtain appropriate security clearance required for the position.

Nice to have

Experience in defence, military communications, command-and-control systems, aerospace, naval systems, UAVs, or other mission-critical operational environments.

· Prior exposure to NATO communication standards, tactical networks, joint fires, air defence, command posts, or battlefield management systems.

· Experience with SATCOM terminals, tactical radios, MANET, IP-based tactical networks, or professional communication equipment.

· Experience integrating unmanned systems into wider military communication architectures.

· Understanding of network security, encryption concepts, authentication, routing, IP networking, and secure data exchange.

description:

About the team

The Data Operations team owns the entire data lifecycle behind STARK's AI stack: collection, acquisition, generation, curation, and management. We run our own data-collection campaigns across Europe, evaluate new sensors and platforms, and build the internal data platform that turns raw recordings into ready-to-use datasets. Everything we produce feeds directly into the perception and autonomy systems deployed on STARK's platforms — a real data advantage is built, not bought. The team is scaling up right now: real scope, direct impact, no legacy.

Your mission

You own our data-collection flights. When the perception team needs a specific dataset — a new camera at a new angle, a lidar over specific terrain, a thermal sensor at dusk — you plan the campaign, configure and tune the platform, fly the mission, and bring clean data home. Our hardware engineer builds the rigs and mounts, our robotics engineer makes the sensors record — you make it all fly, reliably, again and again. This is a role for someone with real stick time and real PX4/ArduPilot depth: not a desk job with occasional field trips, but the other way around.

Responsibilities

- Plan and execute field data-collection campaigns across Europe: flight planning, site assessment, pre-flight checks, piloting, logging, and post-flight data offload

- Configure, tune, and troubleshoot PX4/ArduPilot flight stacks for stable, repeatable data-collection flights

- Analyze flight logs to diagnose issues and continuously improve platform reliability

- Operate sensor payloads (cameras, gimbals, lidar, GNSS/IMU) during missions and verify recordings on-site

- Keep the fleet mission-ready: maintenance, repairs, spare parts, battery management, and configuration control

- Work with our hardware and robotics engineers on payload integration — you define what the platform needs to fly well

- Maintain flight logs and campaign documentation so every flight produces usable, traceable data

- Ensure operations comply with aviation regulations (EU drone rules) and internal safety procedures

Qualifications

- Confident, experienced drone pilot with substantial real-world flight hours (multirotor; fixed-wing a plus), holding an EU A2/A3 certificate or willing to obtain quickly

- Solid practical knowledge of PX4 and/or ArduPilot: configuration, parameter tuning, log analysis, MAVLink basics

- Hands-on experience assembling, repairing, and maintaining drones — comfortable with soldering, wiring, and multimeter debugging

- Experience operating sensor payloads and ground control stations in the field

- Practical, structured, and safety-conscious — you find the loose cable before it becomes a crash

- Willingness to travel regularly for field campaigns and work outdoors in various conditions

- Good communication skills in English (German is a plus)

Nice to have

- Scripting skills (Python, Bash) for flight log processing and data offload automation

- CAD basics (Fusion 360, SolidWorks) and 3D-printing experience

- Experience with ROS/ROS2 recording setups or companion computers (Jetson, Raspberry Pi)

- Background in FPV, drone racing, RC modeling, competition teams, or maker culture

- Experience with camera settings and image quality trade-offs for data collection

- German driving license class B (field campaigns)

A note on our process: a portfolio says more than a CV here. Show us your builds and your flights — photos, flight logs, competition entries. If you don't hit every bullet point but you have been flying and fixing drones for years, we still want to hear from you.
If you're interested in building the future of European Defence with us, please send us your CV and portfolio in English. We're looking forward to meeting you!
